Services

Partnership setup and annual returns

A partnership is two or more people carrying on a business together. It gets its own TFN, ABN and tax return, but it pays no tax itself — the profit is split and each partner declares their share at their own rate.

Our fee

Quoted before we start

Fixed, agreed in writing, no work begins before you accept it.

Government charges

None

A partnership TFN and ABN are free. You pay us for the structure decision and the agreement, not the lodgement.

Who does it

A registered tax agent

BRS Advisory Pty Ltd, agent 26233684, CPA Australia Practice.

What’s included

  • Whether a partnership is right, or whether a company or trust fits what you are actually doing
  • Partnership TFN and ABN
  • GST registration where turnover reaches the $75,000 threshold
  • A written partnership agreement — profit split, decisions, and what happens when someone leaves
  • Annual partnership return, with the distribution statement for each partner
  • Each partner’s individual return, with their share picked up correctly

How it runs

  1. 01 Tell us who is in, what each person is contributing, and how you intend to split the profit.
  2. 02 We check a partnership is the right structure — it is cheap and simple, and it also carries joint liability.
  3. 03 Registrations go in, and the agreement is drafted so the split is written down before there is anything to argue about.
  4. 04 Each year the partnership return is lodged, and each partner’s share flows through to their own return.

What a partnership is and isn’t

A partnership lodges a return so the ATO can see how the profit was split, but it does not pay tax on it. Each partner picks up their share and is taxed at their own marginal rate, which is often the whole appeal — two people on lower rates beat one person on a higher one.

The trade-off is liability. In a general partnership each partner can be pursued for the whole of the partnership’s debts, not just their share, and that includes debts the other partner ran up. It is the usual reason people move to a company or a trust later, and it is considerably cheaper to think about now.

Start it

Tell us who is involved and what the business does, and we will come back with a fixed fee and what we need from you.

Form not loading? Open it in a new tab, or call 0407 179 179 and we will take the details over the phone. Please don’t include your tax file number either way — we ask for it securely once an accountant is working on your file.

Work the numbers first

  • Sole trader

    Tax on business profit, plus what to put aside for GST and the next PAYG instalment.

  • GST

    Add or remove GST, and see the GST-exclusive figure your BAS actually wants.

Registered tax agent

A real practice, not a form that emails you a PDF

Every return is prepared and reviewed by a registered agent before it is lodged. Because we lodge on your behalf, you get the agent deadline rather than the 31 October one — that is roughly six extra months, and it is the single most common reason people switch.
